Corpus français de presse historique PressMint-FR [PressMint.ana SAMPLE]

bibl.title: BnF/Gallica OCR data for Le Temps
Donnees OCR BnF/Gallica pour Le Temps

projectDesc.p: PressMint is a project that aims to (1) create a multilingual set of corpora of historical newspapers uniformly encoded according to the PressMint encoding guidelines; (2) add linguistic annotations to the corpora; and (3) make the corpora available through concordancers.

editorialDecl.p: OCR text is preserved without correction, except for whitespace normalisation and line-end hyphen handling.
Line-end hyphenation is resolved using ALTO SUBS_TYPE and SUBS_CONTENT attributes where available. Where not available, the hyphen is preserved.

ALTO TextBlocks are encoded as TEI paragraphs. A block that ends with a line-end hyphen and is followed by a block starting in lowercase is joined to it in one paragraph. No article or section divisions are inferred, because the source contains no logical structMap.
Page order is derived from the METS physical structMap ORDER attribute. ALTO PHYSICAL_IMG_NR is not used (it is 1 on all pages in this dataset).
Text in an issue is encoded in ALTO reading order. No column-aware geometric reordering is applied.Image references use Gallica IIIF URLs because the master TIFF images are not included.

In this linguistically analysed version, the paragraphs are segmented into sentences, and these into words and punctuation marks, with lemmas and UD part-of-speech tags and features, and named entities (PER, LOC, ORG, MISC) are marked. The annotation is applied to uncorrected OCR text and is therefore unreliable where the OCR is poor.

application.label: spaCy fr_core_news_md
application.desc: Tokenisation, sentence segmentation, part-of-speech tagging, morphological analysis and lemmatisation with the spaCy model fr_core_news_md (model version 3.7.0, LGPL-LR), available from https://spacy.io/models/fr.

application.label: historical-ner-baseline
application.desc: Named entity recognition with the model emanuelaboros/historical-ner-baseline (BERT fine-tuned on HIPE-2022 historical newspaper data). Its labels pers, loc, org and prod are mapped to PER, LOC, ORG and MISC; time and scope labels are not used.
